subject: Prompt set and model-fit follow-up - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Taylor <jamie.taylor@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt set and model-fit follow-up - Acme Corp

Hi Jamie - thanks again for the demo and time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Goal we heard: generate product descriptions and short marketing blurbs from structured feature lists, with strict PII redaction and consistent brand tone.
- Primary success metrics: 95% redact-sensitive-fields, mean preference score >= 4.2 on internal evals, latency < 250ms (95th).

Request: to run a focused model-fit evaluation we need a representative prompt set from your side. Can you share: 
1) ~150-300 customer prompts (input feature lists + desired output examples) - include edge cases (partial features, non-English snippets, intentionally misspelled inputs).
2) Any existing redaction rules or examples you want applied (PII patterns, product codes to remove).
3) A short list of expected failure modes or quality trade-offs you care most about.

We can accept a CSV (columns: prompt_id, input_features, expected_output, notes). Attached is a quick template and guidance doc we use for other customers. If it's easier, drop a smaller sample first and we can iterate.

Model recommendations (quick hit, we can tune after we see prompts):
- Redwood-1-small-8k: cost-efficient baseline for qualitative checks
- Redwood-2-medium-16k: better for tone consistency and length; recommend for benchmarks
- For production, consider quantized variants (q2_K) if you need lower cost - we'll provide performance profile.

I'll loop in Logan (ML) and Ben (Solutions) to scope the eval and redaction checklist. Proposed timeline: share prompts by Thu (9/16) -> we run basic model-fit eval by Mon (9/20) -> sync to review.

Thanks - Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Jamie Taylor <jamie.taylor@acme.com>

Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Prompt set and model-fit follow-up - Acme Corp

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the clear recap. We're aligned on goals. Attached is a first pass of ~60 sample prompts (acme_prompt_samples.csv) - a mix of happy-path and edge cases. Notes below: 

- Edge cases included: short/fragment inputs, multilingual (EN/ES), inputs with SKU-like codes (e.g., SKU: XJ-992), and some intentionally redacted outputs we use for internal testing.
- Redaction rules: remove email addresses and US SSN-like strings; mask product codes when requested (we can flag rows with mask=true).
- Known tricky area: when feature lists are ambiguous (e.g., missing "size"), we often see hallucinated defaults - we'd like guidance on how the model should respond (e.g., ask a clarification or default to 'unknown').

Can you confirm the CSV columns you prefer? We used: prompt_id, input_features, expected_output, mask_product_code (true/false), notes.

Attachment: acme_prompt_samples.csv (CSV)

Happy to hop on a quick 20m call if it's helpful.

Cheers,
Jamie

Thanks Jamie - that format looks great and the sample is very useful. A few clarifications and next steps: 

- CSV columns: prompt_id, input_features, expected_output, mask_product_code, language, notes - that will cover edge case tagging.
- Redaction guidance: we recommend flagging any fields containing email/SSN-like patterns and adding a 'redact:true' column for those rows. For product codes we can either mask or map to a safe token depending on whether you want to preserve SKU-level routing.
- Clarification behavior: default policy in our eval harness is to prefer a short clarification question when input is ambiguous. We can configure to default to 'unknown' instead if you prefer. Please indicate preference in the notes column.

Model / benchmark links: 
- Quick model-fit report (will be generated after we run the sample): https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/acme/model-fit-report-v1 
- Internal eval harness & scoring rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePromptCollection (Marissa has shared a folder with the template & rubric)

Logan & Ben - can you take point on a lightweight eval run after Jamie uploads the full set? Key ask: run Redwood-2-medium-16k and Redwood-1-small-8k, capture: accuracy/redaction rate, preference score, and latency profile. Also add a 'regression check' comparing to Redwood baseline we used for similar customers.

Jamie - when you push the full set, please include a short note on which rows are sensitive and any rows you want excluded from internal logging (we'll treat those per your guidance).

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: Eval plan + regression checks for Acme

Marissa / Ben - quick internal note after seeing the sample. Observations & proposed plan: 

- Sample seems to surface the typical hallucination case when features are underspecified. We'll add a separate metric for 'clarification prompts' to quantify when model asks vs. fabricates.
- Redaction: we'll run deterministic regex scrubbers first (emails, SSN patterns) then compare model-level redaction rates. If model-level redaction < 95% we'll apply a post-process mask for production.

- Regression checks: compare Redwood-2-medium-16k vs Redwood-1-small-8k on preference score and redaction rate. Keep an eye on tail latency (95th).

Deliverables: 
1) quick-run (baseline) by EOD Mon (9/20) with a short summary doc (eval_plan_internal.md).
2) follow-up call to review results (30m) - prefer Tue 9/21 afternoon.

I'll start the harness once Jamie uploads the full set and indicates any rows to exclude from logging.

-Logan

1) Please push the full CSV to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePromptCollection and mark any rows with PII or 'no-logging' in the notes column. We'll honor those flags and exclude them from internal logging.
